Healthcare SEO • Medical Marketing • AI Search

Healthcare SEO & Medical Marketing Agency for Doctors and Medical Practices

FixWebsiteIssues.com, the technical SEO and healthcare marketing division of WevTEC, helps physicians, specialists, clinics, dental practices, urgent care centers, freestanding emergency rooms, and multi-location medical groups get found by the right patients. We combine medical SEO, Local SEO and Google Maps, technical website optimization, patient-intent content, Google Ads, and AI Search Optimization around the way patients actually search for symptoms, conditions, treatments, specialists, and nearby care. Houston-based since 2013, serving medical practices nationwide, with the goal of qualified patient inquiries rather than traffic for its own sake.

Houston-Based, Serving Practices Nationwide | Medical SEO + Technical SEO + Google Ads + AI Search | Working With Healthcare Practices Since 2013

Get a Free Medical Practice Visibility Audit
Talk With a Healthcare SEO Specialist
How a patient finds a practice
1
Symptom"why does my heart race randomly" → educational content
2
Condition and treatment"AFib treatment options" → condition and treatment pages

Outcome: a call, an appointment request, or a form, tracked and attributed

What Can We Help Your Medical Practice Improve?

Eight areas, each tied to a specific way patients find and choose a provider. Most engagements combine three or four of them; the audit tells us which.

Healthcare SEO

Increase search relevance for specialties, services, procedures, conditions, and the patient-intent searches that lead to appointments.

Local SEO & Google Maps

Strengthen location signals, physician and practice relationships, and Google Business Profile health so the practice appears where patients search locally.

Medical Content Strategy

Service, condition, procedure, physician, location, and educational content planned from how patients describe their symptoms and needs.

Technical SEO

Fix indexing, crawlability, site architecture, page speed, internal linking, and structured data so strong medical content is not hidden by a weak website.

Healthcare Google Ads

Paid search built around high-intent service and specialty searches, with the landing pages, call tracking, and policy awareness medical campaigns require.

Medical Website Conversion

Improve calls, appointment requests, forms, mobile usability, and the path from a service page to a booked visit.

AI Search Optimization

Structure content, entity information, and authority signals so the practice is more likely to be understood and referenced by Google AI, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Copilot.

Analytics & Search Visibility

Track qualified organic visibility, Google Business Profile actions, tracked calls, form submissions, and the outcomes that matter to the practice.

What Is Healthcare SEO?

Healthcare SEO is the process of improving how easily patients can find a medical practice when they search for doctors, specialists, conditions, treatments, procedures, or healthcare services online. It combines technical SEO, medically responsible content, local visibility, physician and location optimization, reputation signals, and conversion strategy so that a relevant search connects with the right practice, and the visit turns into a call or an appointment request.

Medical SEO is not adding keywords to a doctor’s website. It requires understanding five things at once: what the patient means by the words they use, which specialty and service actually answer that need, whether the search is local, what makes a patient trust a provider they have never met, and whether the website can technically be found and used. A practice that gets four of those right and misses the fifth still loses the patient.

What a complete medical SEO program typically includes

  • Technical SEO: crawlability, indexing, speed, mobile usability, and clean architecture
  • Specialty and service architecture that mirrors how patients search
  • Physician and provider pages that carry credentials and specialty associations
  • Location pages for each office, with distinct content
  • Condition, procedure, and treatment pages written in patient language, reviewed for accuracy
  • Medically responsible educational content that guides rather than diagnoses
  • Local SEO and Google Business Profile management, including practitioner listings
  • Internal linking that connects symptoms, conditions, services, physicians, and locations
  • Structured data that reflects visible content
  • Authority and corroboration: reviews, directories, associations, and citations
  • Content freshness, conversion paths, and analytics tied to patient inquiries

Looking for marketing organized by specialty or city? See our healthcare marketing hub, with pages for gastroenterology, cardiology, plastic surgery and 15 other specialties.

Why one “services” page is rarely enough

A cardiology practice with a single “Cardiology Services” page is competing for chest pain, palpitations, AFib, hypertension, heart failure, stress testing, and echocardiography with one URL. Patients search those individually. Each needs its own page, written in the patient’s words, linked to the physician who treats it and the office where it happens. That structure, not the keyword, is what healthcare SEO is.

Healthcare SEO vs. Medical Marketing: What Is the Difference?

Healthcare SEO is the organic-discovery discipline: earning visibility in Google Search, Google Maps, and AI-assisted search without paying per click. Medical marketing is the broader program that may also include Google Ads, landing pages, content strategy, reputation, website conversion, analytics, and patient acquisition planning. A practice may need only one; most growing practices need both, coordinated so paid and organic do not compete for the same searches.

FixWebsiteIssues delivers either on its own or as one combined program, depending on the practice’s stage, competition, and budget. The table shows where each discipline does its work.

AreaHealthcare SEOMedical marketing
GoalBe found organically for specialty, condition, treatment, and local searchesAcquire qualified patients across every channel, paid and organic
ChannelsGoogle Search, Google Maps, Bing, AI Overviews and assistantsSEO plus Google Ads, landing pages, reputation, website conversion, analytics
Time to effectMonths; compounds over timePaid channels can produce inquiries in weeks while SEO builds
Core workTechnical SEO, architecture, content, local signals, physician and location pages, schemaCampaign strategy, budget allocation, landing pages, call tracking, conversion testing, reporting
Measured byNon-brand organic visibility, Maps actions, organic calls and formsCost per qualified inquiry, blended patient acquisition, channel contribution
Best fitEstablished practices building durable visibility for their specialtiesNew locations, new service lines, competitive procedures, or practices that need volume now

How Patients Search for Doctors and Medical Services

Patients rarely start with “cardiologist near me.” They start with a symptom, move to a condition, compare treatments, look for the right kind of specialist, then narrow to someone nearby who is accepting patients and takes their insurance. Each stage uses different words and is best answered by a different kind of page. A practice that only targets the last stage is absent for most of the journey, which is where competitors and health portals earn the patient’s trust first.

Patient search stageExample searchesBest supporting asset
Symptom discovery"why does my heart race randomly", "stomach pain after eating", "joint stiffness in the morning"Educational content that explains possibilities and when to see a doctor, without diagnosing
Condition research"AFib treatment options", "what is GERD", "rheumatoid arthritis vs osteoarthritis"Condition page linked to the treatments and the specialist who provides them
Treatment or procedure research"cardiac ablation recovery", "colonoscopy prep", "robotic hernia repair", "dental implant cost"Treatment or procedure page with candidacy, what to expect, and next steps
Specialist search"cardiologist for AFib", "gastroenterologist for acid reflux", "surgeon for gallbladder removal"Specialty page and physician profiles with credentials and focus areas
Local intent"cardiologist in Sugar Land", "urgent care open now", "dentist Katy TX"Location page plus a complete, accurate Google Business Profile
Provider evaluation"cardiologist accepting new patients", "does Dr. X take Blue Cross", reviewsPhysician and location content with insurance, hours, and how to book
Conversational AI"who should I see for recurring palpitations", "what kind of doctor treats leg swelling"Clear, answer-first content with consistent entity information an AI system can retrieve and cite

The same pattern holds in every specialty we work with. A primary care patient moves from “annual physical” to “same-day appointment” to “family doctor accepting new patients.” An urgent care patient collapses the journey into one stage: “open now, near me, do they take my insurance.” A dental patient may research veneers for weeks before searching for a cosmetic dentist. Strong healthcare SEO supports the whole journey, and it is honest about which stages a given practice can realistically win.

Healthcare SEO Services for Medical Practices

Fifteen disciplines that make up a complete program. Each is described by what it does for the practice, because a list of labels tells a physician nothing.

Medical SEO Strategy

A written plan tying each specialty, service, and location to the searches it should win, in priority order, with the pages, content, and technical work required to get there. It is the document every other task refers back to.

Technical Healthcare SEO

Crawlability, indexing, speed, mobile usability, canonicalization, redirects, and structured data. Medical sites accumulate technical debt from EHR integrations, patient portals, and past agencies; we find and fix what is hiding your content from Google.

Local SEO for Doctors

Location relevance for each office: consistent name, address, and phone across the web, location pages with real content, local citations, and the review signals that decide who appears in the map pack.

Google Business Profile Optimization

Categories, services, hours, photos, appointment links, Q&A, and posts kept accurate and complete, with practitioner listings managed so physicians and the practice reinforce rather than compete with each other.

Physician & Provider Page Optimization

Provider pages that carry credentials, board certifications, conditions treated, procedures performed, languages, locations, and insurance, structured so both a patient and a search engine can connect the doctor to the care.

Medical Service Page Optimization

Service pages rewritten to match the words patients use, with what the service is, who it is for, what to expect, which providers offer it, and where, plus a clear next step.

Condition & Symptom Content Strategy

Educational content that answers what patients ask at the start of their search, guides them toward appropriate care without diagnosing, and links to the relevant condition, treatment, and specialist pages.

Procedure Page Optimization

Procedure pages that address candidacy, preparation, recovery, risks in plain language, cost or insurance questions where appropriate, and how to schedule a consultation.

Location SEO

Distinct pages for every office with unique content, local landmarks and parking where useful, the providers who practice there, and services available at that site, avoiding the duplicate-page problem that plagues multi-location groups.

Internal Linking

A deliberate link structure among symptoms, conditions, treatments, procedures, physicians, and locations so search engines understand the relationships and patients can move naturally through the journey.

Schema & Entity Optimization

Structured data for the practice, physicians, locations, services, and FAQs, implemented only where it reflects visible content, and entity consistency across the site, Google Business Profile, directories, and licensing boards.

Medical Content Marketing

Ongoing publication of patient-education, seasonal, and specialty content planned from search data, written in patient-friendly language, and reviewed by the practice for accuracy before publishing.

Conversion Optimization

Clear phone and appointment CTAs, fast forms, insurance and hours visibility, mobile usability, and page-level testing so a ranking becomes an inquiry.

Healthcare Google Ads

High-intent service and specialty campaigns with location targeting, negative keywords, policy-compliant ad copy, dedicated landing pages, and call and form conversion tracking.

Search Visibility Reporting

Monthly reporting on non-brand organic visibility, Maps actions, tracked calls, forms, Ads conversions, and technical health, written for a practice administrator, not an SEO.

Local SEO and Google Maps Optimization for Medical Practices

Local SEO matters in healthcare because most patients choose a provider they can reach, and Google Maps is where that choice is made for “near me”, “open now”, and city-plus-specialty searches. Maps visibility depends on the practice’s Google Business Profile, the consistency of its information across the web, the relevance of its website, its reviews, and proximity to the searcher. A practice can rank well in organic results and be invisible in the map pack, or the reverse.

Why physician and practice listings are harder than ordinary local listings

A retail store has one listing. A medical group may have a practice listing per location plus a practitioner listing for each physician, and Google allows both. Left unmanaged, those listings compete with one another, carry conflicting hours and phone numbers, or point to the wrong location. A physician who leaves keeps a listing that still ranks. Duplicate listings created by staff or directories split reviews. Managing practitioner and practice listings as one system, with clear relationships and consistent data, is where most of our local SEO time goes for medical clients.

We do not promise map-pack positions. Proximity is a factor no agency controls. What we can do is remove every reason Google has to prefer a competitor: incomplete categories, inconsistent addresses, unanswered reviews, missing services, wrong hours, and location pages that say nothing.

What local SEO for a medical practice covers

  • Google Business Profile setup, verification, and ongoing management
  • Accurate name, address, phone, and hours everywhere they appear
  • Primary and secondary categories matched to specialty
  • Practitioner listings linked correctly to the practice and location
  • Services and appointment links on the profile
  • Office and location pages with distinct, useful content
  • Review generation guidance and review responses
  • Local citations and directory consistency
  • Duplicate and conflicting listing cleanup
  • Call tracking implemented without breaking listing consistency
  • Local landing pages for service areas where warranted
  • Maps visibility monitoring by location and query

Medical Content Built Around Patient Search Intent

Medical content strategy assigns a page type to each stage of the patient journey: educational articles for symptoms, condition pages for research, treatment and procedure pages for decisions, specialty and physician pages for choosing a provider, and location pages for finding one. Each type has a different job, a different reader, and a different set of searches, and they are linked so a patient can move from any one to the next.

The page types, and why they cannot be merged

A symptom article (“shortness of breath when lying down”) explains what the symptom can mean, when it warrants a visit, and when it warrants emergency care. It does not diagnose. A condition page (“heart failure”) explains the condition, how it is evaluated, and how the practice treats it. A treatment page (“medication management for heart failure”) and a procedure page (“echocardiogram”) address candidacy, expectations, and scheduling. A specialty page (“cardiology”) is the hub that links all of these together. A physician bio carries credentials, focus areas, and the conditions and procedures that doctor handles, and is often the page a patient reads last before calling. A location page answers where, when, and how to get there.

Patient language without medical inaccuracy

Patients search “heart flutter”, not “paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia”. The page must use the patient’s words in headings and openings while staying clinically accurate in the body, and every condition, treatment, and procedure page we write is reviewed by the practice before it goes live. Copied or AI-generated medical content that nobody at the practice has read creates trust and quality problems that outweigh any ranking benefit.

Our guides on medical schema for doctors, E-E-A-T for medical websites, and content gaps on healthcare sites go deeper on this.

Example

What a cardiology content map looks like

Instead of one “Cardiology Services” page, a practice that wants to be found across the patient journey needs pages for the searches patients actually make:

  • Symptoms: chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, leg swelling, dizziness
  • Conditions: AFib, hypertension, heart failure, coronary artery disease, high cholesterol
  • Diagnostics: echocardiogram, stress test, Holter monitor, cardiac CT
  • Treatments: ablation, medication management, cardiac rehab
  • Providers: each cardiologist with the conditions and procedures they focus on
  • Locations: each office, with the providers and services available there

Every symptom page links to its likely conditions; every condition links to its treatments and the physicians who provide them; every physician links to their locations. That web of links is what tells Google, and an AI system, that this practice is the answer.

Healthcare Marketing Requires a Higher Standard of Trust

Medical websites are judged more strictly than most, by patients and by search quality systems, because the consequences of bad information are higher. Google’s quality guidelines single out health topics as ones where experience, expertise, authoritativeness, and trustworthiness matter most. That is not a ranking switch you flip; it is a set of practical signals a practice either has on its site or does not.

We treat the items on the right as requirements, not extras. Most are inexpensive. Most are missing on the medical sites we audit.

  • Physician credentials and biographiesBoard certification, training, focus areas, and a real photo on every provider page.
  • Accurate services and locationsWhat is offered, where, by whom, and with which hours and insurance.
  • Condition and treatment accuracyReviewed by the practice; sourced to reputable references where claims are made.
  • Medical reviewer transparencyFor in-depth educational content, name who reviewed it and when.
  • Authorship and datesWho wrote it, who is accountable, and when it was last updated.
  • Patient-friendly languageClear enough for a worried patient, accurate enough for a clinician.
  • Appropriate disclaimersEducational content is not a diagnosis; emergencies go to 911 or the ER.
  • Privacy-sensitive formsAppointment and contact forms that do not over-collect and are handled appropriately.
  • No overstated claimsOutcomes, safety, and “best” language kept within what can be supported.
  • Reviews handled honestlyResponded to, never fabricated, never filtered.

Technical SEO for Medical Websites

Technical SEO is the work that lets Google crawl, render, index, and trust a medical website. When it fails, excellent clinical content simply does not appear, and the practice usually has no idea why. This is the part of healthcare marketing where FixWebsiteIssues has its deepest history: the company began as a website repair service and still fixes broken, hacked, and de-indexed sites every week.

Medical websites have particular technical risks. Patient portals and scheduling widgets inject scripts that slow pages or hide content. Provider directories generate thousands of thin, near-duplicate URLs. Migrations between agencies leave redirect chains and orphaned pages. A staging site gets indexed. A well-meaning plugin adds a noindex to the entire blog. Each of these is invisible from the front end and fatal for search.

Technical work is done by our own engineers rather than handed off. Where a site needs deeper repair first, our SEO repair, hacked website repair, and website maintenance teams handle it, and for Houston-area practices our Houston website maintenance plans keep it fixed.

What the technical audit covers

  • Crawlability and robots.txt
  • Indexability and accidental noindex
  • XML sitemap accuracy
  • Canonicalization
  • Redirects and redirect chains
  • Duplicate provider and location pages
  • Page speed and Core Web Vitals
  • Mobile usability
  • JavaScript rendering of key content
  • Structured data validity
  • Internal links and orphan pages
  • Broken links and 404s
  • Migration damage
  • HTTPS and mixed content
  • Server reliability and uptime
  • Image optimization and alt text
  • Page templates and layout shift
  • Tag, archive, and pagination bloat
  • AI crawler access (Google, Bing, OpenAI, Perplexity)
  • Security state and malware

AI Search Optimization for Doctors and Medical Practices

AI Search Optimization for healthcare is the work of making a practice’s information clear, consistent, crawlable, and corroborated enough that AI-assisted search systems can understand what the practice does, who its physicians are, where it is, and which patient questions it answers, so it is more likely to be retrieved and referenced when a patient asks. It does not guarantee a mention in ChatGPT, Gemini, or an AI Overview. No agency can. It improves the odds by removing the reasons a system would skip the practice.

Patients now ask complete questions instead of typing fragments: What type of doctor treats recurring palpitations? Should I see a gastroenterologist for stomach pain after eating? Who treats rheumatoid arthritis in Katy? What kind of surgeon repairs an inguinal hernia? Which specialist should I see for leg swelling? Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode, Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Perplexity answer those by retrieving and synthesizing web pages. A practice whose site states plainly that Dr. Smith, a board-certified cardiologist at the Sugar Land office, evaluates palpitations and performs ablation, and whose directory listings agree, gives those systems something to work with. A site with a “Services” page and a contact form does not.

What healthcare AI visibility depends on

  • Clear entity relationships: practice, physicians, specialties, locations, services, all named consistently
  • Understandable physician information: credentials, focus areas, and affiliations in readable text
  • Condition-to-treatment-to-specialist relationships made explicit through content and links
  • Concise, direct answers to the questions patients actually ask
  • Accurate, consistent location and contact information across the web
  • Crawlable content, with AI crawlers allowed where the practice wants visibility
  • Structured data that matches visible content, used as support rather than substitute
  • First-party expertise: the practice’s own observations, criteria, and explanations
  • External corroboration: reviews, directories, board listings, hospital affiliations, press
  • Factual clarity and the absence of overstated claims

We deliver this through the same disciplines as our cross-industry AI Search Optimization practice, applied to medical entities: Generative Engine Optimization for citation-worthiness, Answer Engine Optimization for question-level content, LLM Optimization for entity accuracy, and Google AI Optimization aligned with Google’s own guidance. The starting point is always an AI Visibility Audit that records what these systems say about the practice today.

Google Search, Google Maps, and AI Search Are Different Discovery Environments

They share a foundation but reward different things. A practice that treats them as one channel usually wins none of them well.

Google Organic Search

Ranks web pages by relevance, quality, and authority for a query. Rewards clean technical SEO, pages that match patient intent, strong internal structure, and credible content. Measured in Search Console by query and page.

Google Maps

Ranks local entities, not pages. Depends on the Google Business Profile, proximity to the searcher, categories, reviews, and consistency of the practice’s information across the web. The website supports it; it does not replace it.

Google AI Overviews / Gemini

Compose an answer from Google’s index and link to supporting pages. Favor factual clarity, accessible content, clear entity understanding, and answer-oriented passages. Same fundamentals as Search, with a premium on being quotable.

ChatGPT / Conversational Search

Answers natural-language provider questions by combining what the model learned with live retrieval, often from Bing’s index. Depends on corroborated business information, contextual relevance, and content that answers the question directly.

Healthcare SEO by Medical Specialty

Every specialty has its own patient vocabulary, journey length, and competitive set. These are the specialties we work in, with the search patterns that shape the strategy for each. Where a dedicated resource exists, the card links to it.

Cardiology SEO

Chest pain, palpitations, AFib, hypertension, heart failure, vascular testing, and diagnostic searches, mapped to condition, procedure, and cardiologist pages.

Cardiology SEO tips →

Gastroenterology SEO

Stomach pain, acid reflux, colonoscopy, endoscopy, IBS and digestive conditions, GI specialist searches, and self-pay procedure pricing where applicable.

Preventive care, chronic disease management, annual visits, same-day and new-patient searches, and the local PCP queries that decide where a family goes.

Experience Across Healthcare Search and Medical Practice Marketing

The verticals below reflect the healthcare organizations FixWebsiteIssues and WevTEC currently support with SEO, technical website management, and marketing. Client names and results are shared only with permission; the descriptions cover the kinds of problems handled in each.

Emergency Room & Urgent Care

Freestanding ERs and urgent care centers in Houston and Texas: open-now and symptom intent, location pages, Google Business Profile accuracy, hours and insurance visibility, technical fixes on high-traffic sites, and Google Ads under healthcare policy constraints.

Cardiology & Vascular

Cardiology and vein/vascular practices: symptom-to-condition-to-procedure architecture, physician pages, diagnostic service pages, local search across multiple offices, and AI-readiness of entity information.

Gastroenterology

Google Ads for Doctors and Medical Practices

Google Ads lets a practice appear immediately for high-intent searches while SEO builds, and it is the right tool for new locations, new service lines, competitive procedures, and seasonal demand. It is not right for every practice, and it wastes money fast when the landing page, targeting, and tracking are wrong.

Healthcare campaigns carry constraints other industries do not: Google’s healthcare and medicines policies restrict certain ad content, remarketing to people based on health conditions is not permitted, and symptom-based targeting has to be handled carefully so the ad is helpful rather than alarming. Our guide to Google Ads healthcare campaign restrictions covers the practical rules.

What makes a medical campaign efficient is specificity: one campaign per service line or procedure, tight geographic targeting around each office, dedicated landing pages that match the ad, negative keywords that remove job seekers and researchers, call tracking and appointment-form conversions, and weekly search-term review. We run Ads alongside SEO so the two channels are measured against the same qualified-inquiry goal rather than competing for the same clicks.

  • Negative keyword lists built for medical searches
  • Symptom searches only where an ad is appropriate

Turning Search Visibility Into Patient Inquiries

A page that ranks and does not produce calls or appointment requests is a cost, not an asset. Conversion work makes sure that when a patient arrives, on a phone, often anxious, the next step is obvious, fast, and reassuring.

The most common failures we find on medical sites are ordinary: the phone number is an image, the appointment button leads to a portal login, insurance is not mentioned, hours are wrong, the form asks twelve questions, the provider page has no photo, and the site takes six seconds to load on a mobile connection. None of these are marketing problems in the usual sense, and all of them decide whether the ranking paid off.

We do not use pressure or fear tactics in medical conversion. Urgency belongs to the patient’s situation, not to the page. Emergency instructions, where appropriate, tell the patient to call 911 or go to the nearest ER before anything else.

What we check and fix on every medical site

  • Click-to-call phone number in the header on mobile
  • A clear request-appointment path that does not require a login
  • Service-specific calls to action on service pages
  • Physician photos, credentials, and focus areas
  • Location, parking, and hours on every location page
  • Insurance accepted, stated plainly
  • Emergency instructions where relevant
  • Short, privacy-conscious forms that actually deliver
  • Accessible navigation and readable type
  • Page speed on mobile connections
  • Trust signals: reviews, affiliations, accreditations

Observations from healthcare sites we audit

These are patterns, not statistics; we have not published a formal study and will not present one until the data is documented.

  • A high-ranking page that produces no appointments almost always has a conversion problem the practice cannot see on desktop: a phone number that is not tappable, a form that fails, or a portal login where a request button should be.
  • Duplicate location pages with the city name swapped are the most common self-inflicted cannibalization on multi-location medical sites.
  • Physician biographies are among the last pages a patient reads before calling and among the least optimized on most sites.
  • Practitioner listings on Google Business Profile are routinely orphaned when a physician leaves, and keep ranking for the old practice.
  • “Near me” repeated in page copy does nothing; Google infers proximity from the searcher, not from the text.
  • Copied or unreviewed AI medical content is easy to spot, by patients and by quality systems, and creates a trust deficit that outweighs any ranking it might earn.

What is healthcare SEO?

Healthcare SEO is the process of improving how easily patients find a medical practice when they search for doctors, specialists, conditions, treatments, procedures, or services online. It combines technical SEO, medically responsible content, local visibility, physician and location optimization, reputation signals, and conversion strategy so relevant searches reach the right practice and turn into inquiries.

How is healthcare SEO different from regular SEO?

Healthcare SEO carries stricter quality expectations, a longer and more emotional patient journey, complex physician and location entity relationships, and advertising and privacy constraints that other industries do not face. Google treats health topics as ones where expertise and trust matter most, and a medical site must match patient language without becoming clinically inaccurate. The technical fundamentals are the same; the standard of care around them is higher.

What does a healthcare SEO agency do?

A healthcare SEO agency audits a practice’s search visibility, researches how patients search for its specialties, fixes the website’s technical issues, builds or improves specialty, service, condition, procedure, physician, and location pages, manages Google Business Profile and local signals, and measures results in qualified patient inquiries. Many, including FixWebsiteIssues, also run Google Ads and AI Search Optimization alongside SEO.

How can SEO help a medical practice get more patients?

SEO puts the practice in front of patients at the moment they are searching for the care it provides, from early symptom research to “accepting new patients” searches. When the pages they land on are clear, trustworthy, and easy to act on, those visits become calls and appointment requests. The gain comes from coverage across the patient journey, not from a single ranking.

How long does medical SEO usually take?

Technical fixes take effect within weeks of Google re-crawling the site. New or rewritten specialty and service pages typically need several months to earn stable visibility, longer in competitive metro markets. Local and Maps improvements often show sooner. Timelines depend on the practice’s starting point and competition and are estimated in the audit, not guaranteed.

What types of doctors benefit from SEO?

Any physician or practice whose patients choose them through search: primary care, cardiology, gastroenterology, rheumatology, orthopedics, general and bariatric surgery, vascular, dermatology, OB/GYN, dental and cosmetic dental, plastic surgery, med spas, urgent care, and emergency rooms. Specialties with long research journeys, such as cardiology or bariatrics, benefit from content depth; immediate-need providers such as urgent care benefit most from local and Maps work.

What is Local SEO for doctors?

Local SEO for doctors is the work of making a practice and its physicians visible for location-based searches, primarily in Google Maps and the local pack. It centers on the Google Business Profile, consistent name, address, and phone data across the web, distinct location pages, categories, reviews, and the relationships between practitioner listings and the practice.

How does Google Maps optimization work for medical practices?

Google Maps ranks local entities based on relevance, distance, and prominence. For a medical practice that means a complete, accurate Google Business Profile with the right categories and services, consistent information across directories, reviews and responses, location pages that support the listing, and correctly managed practitioner listings for each physician. Proximity to the searcher is outside anyone’s control, so the goal is to remove every other reason a competitor would be preferred.

Do physicians need individual SEO pages?

Yes. A physician profile is a search asset in its own right: patients search doctors by name, and search engines use the page to connect the doctor to specialties, conditions, procedures, and locations. A strong profile includes credentials, focus areas, conditions treated, procedures performed, languages, locations, insurance, and a photo, and it links to the services and offices it relates to.

Should medical practices create pages for conditions and symptoms?

Yes, when done responsibly. Condition pages capture patients who are researching a diagnosis; symptom content reaches them earlier and guides them toward appropriate care without diagnosing. Each should link to the relevant treatments and the physicians who provide them. Content should be reviewed by the practice, use patient language, and direct urgent symptoms to emergency care.

Does healthcare SEO include Google Ads?

Not by definition; SEO is organic visibility and Google Ads is paid. FixWebsiteIssues offers both and runs them together when a practice needs immediate volume for a new location, service line, or competitive procedure while SEO builds. Ads for healthcare must follow Google’s healthcare policies, and campaigns are measured on cost per qualified inquiry.

How can a medical practice improve visibility in Google AI Overviews?

By meeting the same fundamentals Google’s documentation says AI features rely on: crawlable, indexable pages; unique, useful content that answers patient questions directly; accurate structured data; good page experience; and clear internal links. No special markup is required and none guarantees inclusion. Pages that state plainly what the practice treats, who treats it, and where are the natural candidates.

Can SEO help a medical practice appear in ChatGPT or Gemini?

It can improve the likelihood. AI assistants retrieve live web pages and rely on consistent, corroborated information about a business. Clear physician and specialty information, consistent entity data across the web, direct answers to common patient questions, and allowed crawler access all help a practice be understood and referenced. No agency can guarantee a mention, and we do not.

What is AI Search Optimization for healthcare?

AI Search Optimization for healthcare is the work of making a practice’s information clear, consistent, crawlable, and corroborated so AI-assisted search systems can understand its physicians, specialties, locations, and services and are more likely to retrieve and reference it when patients ask conversational questions. It builds on healthcare SEO rather than replacing it.

What is GEO for healthcare?

Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) for healthcare is the discipline of becoming the source that generative engines such as Google AI Overviews, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Perplexity retrieve, trust, and cite when composing an answer about a condition, treatment, or provider. For a practice it means specific, verifiable passages, consistent entity information, and outside corroboration such as reviews, directories, and affiliations.

How should a multi-location medical practice structure its website?

With one distinct page per location, each carrying its own address, hours, providers, services available at that site, and unique content; a single page per specialty and service that links to the locations offering it; physician profiles that list every location a doctor practices at; and a Google Business Profile per location with practitioner listings connected correctly. Duplicated location pages with the city name swapped are the most common mistake and should be avoided.

Can you optimize a medical website built by another company?

Yes. Most of our healthcare clients came to us with sites built by other agencies or platforms, including WordPress, Divi, WooCommerce, and custom builds. We document the site, fix the technical foundation, and improve content and structure without requiring a redesign unless one is genuinely warranted.

How do you measure healthcare SEO success?

By qualified patient inquiries and the visibility that produces them: non-brand organic clicks for specialty and service queries, Google Business Profile calls and direction requests, tracked calls and form submissions attributed to source, service and location page conversion rates, Google Ads cost per qualified inquiry where applicable, technical health, and recorded AI visibility observations. Traffic totals alone are not a success measure.
